terms.definition: A typed, validated operation the agent can invoke. Defined by a Zod/JSONSchema input schema, a call() method, concurrency flags, and deferral status. Registered in the tool catalog and dispatched by the tool execution pipeline.
A single-use agent invoked by the parent session via the Agent tool; has a fresh context; returns one result; does not persist across dispatches.
A forked subagent process that runs in isolation from the parent, communicating only through structured input/output. Implemented via forkedAgent.ts and forkSubagent.ts.
A git worktree providing an isolated filesystem copy of the repository for parallel development. Created by EnterWorktreeTool and managed via worktree.ts utilities.
A durable unit of work tracked by the task system (src/utils/tasks.ts). Has status transitions (pending → in_progress → completed), blocking relationships, and filesystem-based storage.
A reusable prompt template or capability loaded from ~/.claude/skills/ or bundled skills. Can be user-invocable or triggered, and may execute inline or in a fork context.
A /-prefixed command typed in the REPL prompt. Dispatched through commands.ts registry and processSlashCommand.tsx. Can be prompt-based or callback-based.

A deterministic lifecycle event handler triggered at specific points (PreToolUse, PostToolUse, etc.). Defined by schemas/hooks.ts and executed via the hooks pipeline. Types: command, prompt, http, agent, function.
A session-level setting governing how tool-use approvals are handled. Modes include default, plan, acceptEdits, bypassPermissions, dontAsk, and auto. Defined in PermissionMode.ts.
A function that maps shell commands to risk bands (read, write, destructive) for the permission system. Implemented in bashClassifier.ts and yoloClassifier.ts.
The process of reducing conversation context size to stay within token limits. The five-stage hierarchy: history_snip → microcompact → context collapse → autocompact → hard reset.
The second stage of compaction. Selectively removes low-value messages while preserving key context. Implemented in microCompact.ts with time-based configuration from timeBasedMCConfig.ts.
The third stage of compaction. A more aggressive context reduction triggered when microcompact is insufficient. Gated behind the CONTEXT_COLLAPSE feature flag.
The fourth stage of compaction. Automatically triggers compaction when token usage approaches limits. Implemented in autoCompact.ts with both proactive and reactive modes.
A persistent knowledge record stored in the memdir filesystem (src/memdir/). Types include user, feedback, project, and reference. Managed through MEMORY.md index files.
The tiered memory-on-disk system at ~/.claude/projects/<id>/memory/. Provides persistent, structured storage for agent knowledge across sessions. Implemented in src/memdir/.
A single invocation of the cc agent, from entry through exit. Stored as JSONL in sessionStorage.ts. Includes messages, tool calls, and metadata.
A five-phase operating mode where the agent explores, plans, and then executes. Read-only enforcement during exploration phase. Implemented via EnterPlanModeTool, ExitPlanModeTool, and planModeV2.ts.
The engineering layer around an LLM that provides tools, memory, permissions, hooks, and lifecycle management. The pattern: Agent = Model + Harness.
An input channel that feeds information into the agent's context. Includes file reads, search results, web content, and user messages. Part of the harness's observation layer.
An output directive from the harness that constrains or shapes the agent's behavior. Includes system prompts, CLAUDE.md instructions, permission rules, and hook responses.
A mechanism that limits the rate of work when downstream systems (API, user, storage) cannot keep up. Implemented via token budgets, rate limiting, and deferral flags.
A tool that is not loaded into the model's context initially, but is discovered on-demand via ToolSearchTool. Implements Pattern 9 Progressive Tool Expansion.
The ToolSearchTool that enables the model to discover and load tools on demand, implementing progressive tool expansion. Prevents context bloat from large tool catalogs.
A hook event type fired before a tool's call() method executes. Allows approval, denial, or modification of tool invocations. Part of the deterministic lifecycle hooks pattern.
A hook event type fired after a tool's call() method completes. Allows post-processing, logging, or conditional actions based on tool results. Part of the deterministic lifecycle hooks pattern.
A structured JSON registry (manifest.json) tracking all chapters, their source files, HER references, diagram requirements, and status throughout the build process.
A multi-agent pattern where one agent generates solutions and another evaluates them. Referenced in HER §9.2. Related to the coordinator's swarm orchestration in cc.
A pattern for saving and restoring agent state across interruptions. Implemented in cc via session JSONL storage. Identified in HER as failure mode 6.16.
The practice of stripping or summarizing observed tool outputs to reduce context size and cost. HER reports 52% cost reduction. Implemented in cc via compaction and microcompact.
